proposed.text: A contractor encloses an existing open terrace to create a new room — adding gross floor area but not height. Under IRR Sec. 106, this is classified as:

options.text: Addition to GFA (enclosed terrace adds floor area)

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Per IRR Sec. 106, an Addition is new construction that increases height and/or floor area. The 'and/or' means increasing EITHER height OR floor area — not necessarily both — constitutes an Addition. Enclosing a terrace increases gross floor area; therefore the work is an Addition, requiring an addition permit. This is a common exam trap where candidates assume both dimensions must change.
proposed.code_citation: PD 1096 IRR, Sec. 106 (Work classifications: Alteration / Addition / Repair / Renovation / Conversion)
